Microsporidiosis Microsporidia are obligate intracellular spore-forming protozoal parasites. They were primarily regarded as a cause of disease in nonhuman species but some, including Encephalitozoon, Enterocytozoon, Pleistophora, and Tra- chipleistophora spp. and Brachiola vesicularum and Vitta- forma corneae (Nosema corneum), are now recognised as human pathogens. Transmission is believed to be predom- inantly faeco-oral although inhalation and direct inocula- tion also occur. Infections usually occur only in immuno- compromised patients. Small bowel infection with Enterocytozoon bieneusi has been reported in AIDS pa- tients as a cause of chronic diarrhoea and weight loss
